services.i0_intro_title: Networking and IT Infrastructure Solutions for Businesses
services.i0_intro_paragraphs_i0: Networking and infrastructure services cover the planning, supply, installation, security and ongoing support of the technology that connects your people, devices and applications. That includes cabling, switches, routers, Wi-Fi, firewalls, servers, storage and the links to cloud services your business relies on.
services.i0_intro_paragraphs_i1: When this layer is planned well, nobody notices it. When it is not, everyone does: video calls drop, files open slowly, new staff wait days for a desk to be connected, and a single failed switch can stall a whole floor.
services.i0_intro_paragraphs_i2: Cloute Technologies helps businesses in India deal with problems such as:
services.i0_intro_list_i0: Wi-Fi that works near the access point and fails in meeting rooms or at the far end of the floor
services.i0_intro_list_i1: A network that grew device by device with no documentation, making faults slow to trace
services.i0_intro_list_i2: Tangled or unlabelled cabling that turns every move or addition into a risk
services.i0_intro_list_i3: Ageing switches, routers or firewalls that cannot handle current traffic or security needs
services.i0_intro_list_i4: Offices or branches that need to connect securely to each other and to cloud applications
services.i0_intro_list_i5: Servers and storage that have outgrown their room, power or backup arrangements
services.i0_intro_list_i6: No clear owner for monitoring, maintenance and fixes after installation
services.i0_intro_after_i0: We work with startups, growing SMEs and enterprise teams. The first step is always the same: understand what your network supports today and what it needs to support next.
services.i0_intro_after_i1: Networking is one part of the wider service range at Cloute. When your project also involves devices, security, cloud or support, we can plan it together. See our [IT hardware range](/products) for routers, switches, servers and storage, or our [cybersecurity services](/cybersecurity-services) for security beyond the network layer.

services.i0_grid_text: Nine services, from first design to ongoing support. You can engage us for a single piece of work or for an end-to-end project.
services.i0_grid_features_i0_problem: Networks that grow without a plan tend to slow down, fail in unexpected places and become hard to secure.
services.i0_grid_features_i0_text: We start by reviewing your current setup: users, devices, applications, locations and the performance gaps people already complain about. From that, we design a network architecture that fits your size and budget, then supply, install and configure it.
services.i0_grid_features_i0_includes_i0: Assessment of the existing network and traffic needs
services.i0_grid_features_i0_includes_i1: Topology, addressing and VLAN planning (VLANs separate one physical network into logical segments, for example staff, guests and CCTV, which improves both performance and security)
services.i0_grid_features_i0_benefit: A network that is easier to run, easier to expand and less likely to fail without warning.
services.i0_grid_features_i1_problem: Teams in different rooms, floors or cities need fast, consistent access to the same systems.
services.i0_grid_features_i1_text: A local area network (LAN) connects devices within one location, such as an office floor or building. A wide area network (WAN) connects multiple locations to each other or to external networks, including the internet. Most growing businesses need both to work together.
services.i0_grid_features_i1_includes_i0: Switching and routing for the office LAN
services.i0_grid_features_i1_includes_i1: Internet link planning and failover options
services.i0_grid_features_i1_includes_i2: Secure links between offices, and secure remote access through VPNs (a VPN encrypts traffic between a user or site and your network)
services.i0_grid_features_i1_includes_i3: Bandwidth planning for cloud, video and file-sharing use
services.i0_grid_features_i1_benefit: Consistent connectivity across sites, with secure access for remote and hybrid staff.
services.i0_grid_features_i2_problem: Poorly organised cabling causes intermittent faults and makes every change slow and risky.
services.i0_grid_features_i2_text: Structured cabling is an organised, standards-based cabling system that runs from a central point, usually a rack or comms room, to every work area. It carries your data, and often voice and video, in a consistent layout.
services.i0_grid_features_i2_includes_i0: Cable routing to desks, meeting rooms and access points
services.i0_grid_features_i2_includes_i1: Racks, patch panels and clear labelling
services.i0_grid_features_i2_includes_i2: Termination and testing of installed links
services.i0_grid_features_i2_includes_i3: Connecting new equipment to the existing network
services.i0_grid_features_i2_benefit: A tidy, documented installation that is faster to troubleshoot and simpler to extend.
services.i0_grid_features_i3_problem: Dead spots, slow speeds in busy areas and poorly separated guest access.
services.i0_grid_features_i3_text: Business Wi-Fi is planned around how many people and devices use each area, the building layout and the applications they run. Where required, a Wi-Fi site survey measures coverage and interference before access points are placed.
services.i0_grid_features_i3_includes_i2: Secure authentication for users and devices
services.i0_grid_features_i3_benefit: Dependable wireless connectivity for laptops, phones and shared devices across the workplace.
services.i0_grid_features_i4_problem: A network without proper controls exposes devices and data to unauthorised access and malware.
services.i0_grid_features_i4_text: We set up and configure the protective layers of your network: firewalls that filter traffic, intrusion prevention systems (IPS) that detect and block suspicious activity, segmentation that limits how far a problem can spread, and encryption for data in transit.
services.i0_grid_features_i4_includes_i0: Firewall selection, installation and rule configuration
services.i0_grid_features_i4_includes_i1: Intrusion prevention and threat detection settings
services.i0_grid_features_i4_includes_i2: Network segmentation and secure remote access
services.i0_grid_features_i4_includes_i3: Review of existing network security settings
services.i0_grid_features_i4_benefit: Reduced exposure to common network threats and clearer control over who and what connects.
services.i0_grid_features_i4_note: No provider can promise zero incidents. Our focus is on sound configuration and ongoing attention. For security services beyond the network, see [Cybersecurity Services](/cybersecurity-services).
services.i0_grid_features_i5_problem: Servers and storage that were added piecemeal become a single point of failure.
services.i0_grid_features_i5_text: We help plan and deploy the server and storage environment that your applications and data depend on, whether that is a server room in your office or a larger setup. Planning covers redundancy (duplicate components so that one failure does not stop the service) and recovery arrangements.

services.i0_grid_features_i5_includes_i2: Backup, redundancy and disaster recovery planning
services.i0_grid_features_i5_includes_i3: Network connectivity between servers, users and cloud services
services.i0_grid_features_i5_benefit: A server environment sized for current needs, with room to grow and a plan for recovery.
services.i0_grid_features_i6_problem: Applications move to the cloud, but the office network is not set up to reach them securely and reliably.
services.i0_grid_features_i6_text: Cloud services are commonly described as IaaS (rented infrastructure), PaaS (a platform to build and run applications) and SaaS (ready-to-use software). A hybrid setup keeps some systems on your own premises and some in the cloud, connected securely.

services.i0_grid_features_i6_includes_i1: Hybrid arrangements for systems that need to stay on-premises
services.i0_grid_features_i6_includes_i2: Support during migration of data and workloads
services.i0_grid_features_i6_benefit: Flexibility to use the cloud without losing control of your network. For migration and cloud management, see [Cloud Services](/cloud-services).

services.i0_grid_features_i7_text: After installation, we can monitor the network, troubleshoot faults and carry out routine maintenance so small issues are fixed before they disrupt work.

services.i0_faqs_i0_q: What are networking and infrastructure services?
services.i0_faqs_i0_a: Networking and infrastructure services are the planning, installation, security and support of the systems that connect a business's computers, applications and data. They typically cover cabling, switches, routers, Wi-Fi, firewalls, servers, storage and connections to the cloud. The aim is a network that is fast, secure and dependable enough that staff do not have to think about it.
services.i0_faqs_i1_q: Which company provides networking and infrastructure services in India?
services.i0_faqs_i1_a: Cloute Technologies, based in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, provides networking and infrastructure services, including network design and implementation, structured cabling, Wi-Fi, firewall and security configuration, server and data center infrastructure, cloud connectivity and network support. Many IT companies across India offer similar services, so compare scope, references and support terms before choosing.
services.i0_faqs_i2_q: What does an IT infrastructure company do?
services.i0_faqs_i2_a: An IT infrastructure company plans, supplies, installs and maintains the core technology a business runs on, such as networks, servers, storage, security systems and cloud connections. Many also provide ongoing monitoring and support after installation.
services.i0_faqs_i3_q: What is the difference between LAN and WAN networking?
services.i0_faqs_i3_a: A LAN (local area network) connects devices within one location, such as an office or building. A WAN (wide area network) connects multiple locations, or links a location to the wider internet. In practice, a company with several offices uses a LAN at each site and a WAN, often secured with VPNs, to connect them.
services.i0_faqs_i4_q: Does Cloute Technologies provide network design and installation?
services.i0_faqs_i4_a: Yes. Cloute Technologies designs, supplies, installs and configures business networks. The work starts with an assessment of your current setup and requirements, followed by a proposed design and quotation, then installation, configuration and testing.
services.i0_faqs_i5_q: Can Cloute upgrade existing office networking infrastructure?
services.i0_faqs_i5_a: Yes. Cloute can review an existing network and upgrade parts of it, such as switches, Wi-Fi, cabling or firewalls, without necessarily replacing everything. We assess what is working, what is limiting performance and what should change first.
services.i0_faqs_i6_q: What is the role of network security in IT infrastructure?
services.i0_faqs_i6_a: Network security controls who and what can reach your systems and data. It typically includes firewalls to filter traffic, intrusion prevention to detect suspicious activity, network segmentation to contain problems and encryption to protect data in transit. No setup removes all risk, so security also needs regular review and updates.
services.i0_faqs_i7_q: How can businesses improve Wi-Fi coverage and network performance?
services.i0_faqs_i7_a: Start by finding where the problems occur: coverage gaps, congested areas or overloaded equipment. Common fixes include repositioning or adding access points based on a coverage survey, upgrading ageing switches and routers, separating guest and staff networks and checking that the internet connection suits current usage. A network assessment shows which of these will make the biggest difference.
services.i0_faqs_i8_q: How do I choose an IT infrastructure services provider?
services.i0_faqs_i8_a: Look for a provider that assesses your needs before recommending products, gives a written scope and quotation, explains its design in plain language and documents what it installs. Ask for relevant references or examples of similar work, how support works after installation, and what warranty and service terms apply to the equipment.

intro.title: Professional IT Support and Helpdesk Services for Businesses
paragraphs: IT support and helpdesk services give your employees one clear place to report technical problems and get them fixed. A helpdesk receives each request, records it as a ticket, works out what is wrong and either resolves it or passes it to someone with the right skills. The related term service desk usually means a broader version that also handles routine requests, such as new user accounts or software access, and follows formal IT service management processes.

Most businesses need this long before they have a full IT department. Without a defined route for problems, work stops while people wait for the colleague who is good with computers, fixes are not recorded and the same issue returns again and again. A dedicated support function gives staff a clear way to ask for help, gives managers a record of what is happening and lets your own IT team focus on projects instead of password resets and printer faults.

Helpdesk support is request-driven: people report problems and they are fixed. If you want a provider to take on the continuous, proactive management of your whole IT environment, that is covered by our [Managed IT Services](/managed-it-services).
list: Slow laptops, operating system errors and devices that will not start
Software that will not install or update

Email that will not configure

after: Structured support brings practical benefits: every request is recorded, urgent issues can be prioritised, the history of a device or user helps diagnose repeat problems and managers can see which issues take the most time.

Support can be delivered remotely, where an engineer connects to a device over the internet, or on-site, where an engineer visits your premises. Many businesses use a mix of both, and the comparison later on this page explains how each works.

solutions.title: Common IT Problems We Help Businesses Resolve
solutions.text: These are the problems businesses bring to a helpdesk most often. Not every issue can be fixed remotely, and some need a physical visit or a part replaced, but most start with the same careful diagnosis.

items.title: Slow computers and laptops
items.text: Causes include full storage, too many startup programs, outdated software, malware or ageing hardware. We check performance, clean up, update and recommend an upgrade if the device is the limit.

items.title: Operating system errors
items.text: Crashes and failed starts can come from corrupted files, bad updates or failing drives. We diagnose the cause, repair or reinstall where appropriate and protect user data first.

items.title: Software installation issues
items.text: Installations fail because of permissions, missing components, licence problems or conflicts. We find the cause, install and configure the software and escalate to the vendor when needed.

items.text: Slow or dropped connections may come from the device, the Wi-Fi, a cable, a switch or the internet line. We test step by step and escalate faults that need deeper work.

items.title: Printer and peripheral problems
items.text: Printers that will not print and scanners that are not detected often come down to drivers, settings, connections or hardware. We check each and replace or reconfigure as needed.

items.title: Email configuration issues
items.text: Email may not send, receive or sync because of wrong settings, full mailboxes or account problems. We correct the configuration on desktops and mobile devices.

items.title: Login and account access problems
items.text: Locked accounts, expired passwords and missing permissions stop people from working. We verify identity, reset access and correct permissions.

items.title: System update failures
items.text: Updates fail because of low storage, interrupted downloads or conflicts. We clear the cause, retry the update and make sure the device is protected.

items.title: Hardware troubleshooting
items.text: Devices that will not start, overheat or make unusual noises need hands-on checks. We identify the faulty component and arrange repair, replacement or warranty service.

items.title: File access and backup issues
items.text: Files may be unreachable because of permissions, network drives or accidental deletion. We restore access, recover files from backup where possible and check that backups are working.

intro.title: Professional Managed IT Services for Businesses
paragraphs: Managed IT services mean handing the ongoing running of your technology to an outside provider. Instead of waiting for something to break, the provider watches your systems, maintains them on a schedule, fixes problems and reports on how things are performing. A company that does this is often called a managed service provider, or MSP.

An MSP usually works to an agreed scope. That scope states which systems are covered, what the provider monitors, which maintenance tasks it carries out, how problems are reported and escalated, and how the provider reports back to you. Because the work is continuous rather than occasional, it suits businesses that depend on their IT every day.

intro.title: Comprehensive Cybersecurity Solutions for Businesses
paragraphs: Cybersecurity services help a business protect its computers, networks, applications and data from unauthorised access, misuse and damage. They include checking where you are exposed, putting protective controls in place, watching for signs of an attack and planning how to respond if one happens.

Security work is usually described in three activities. Prevention reduces the chance that an attack succeeds, for example by applying updates, restricting access and filtering network traffic. Detection finds suspicious activity that gets past prevention, through monitoring and alerts. Response limits the damage and restores normal working once an incident has been confirmed. A sound programme needs all three, because prevention alone will never be complete.

Cybersecurity matters for Indian businesses of every size. Companies hold customer records, financial data and business-critical systems that are valuable to attackers and costly to lose, and smaller businesses are often targeted precisely because they have fewer protections. Remote working, cloud services and personal devices have widened the number of places where something can go wrong.
list: Phishing emails that trick staff into revealing passwords
Ransomware that locks files until a payment is made
Stolen or reused credentials
Software that has not been updated
Cloud services left open by mistake
Staff who have more access than they need
after: Security controls support business continuity by lowering the likelihood of disruption and making recovery faster and better organised. A review done once becomes out of date as soon as you add a new application, office or cloud account, so regular reviews keep controls matched to the environment you actually have.

A good starting point is simple questions: what data and systems matter most, who has access to them, how are devices and networks protected, what happens if a system is locked or data is lost and where are the gaps. We help you work through them.

solutions.text: For awareness and defence: what each threat means for a business and what usually helps.

items.title: Phishing and social engineering
items.text: Convincing emails or messages trick staff into revealing passwords or approving payments. Defences: staff training, email filtering, multi-factor authentication and a clear way to report suspicious messages.

items.title: Ransomware
items.text: Locks or encrypts files and demands payment. Defences: regular updates, restricted access, tested backups kept apart from the main network, endpoint protection and a practised incident plan.

items.title: Malware
items.text: Viruses, spyware and other harmful software, usually arriving through attachments, downloads or infected devices. Defences: endpoint protection, updates and limits on software installation.

items.title: Unauthorized system access
items.text: Someone gets into a system, account or device they should not reach. Defences: strong authentication, least-privilege permissions, network controls and monitoring for unusual logins.

items.title: Credential theft
items.text: Usernames and passwords stolen through phishing or fake login pages, then tried against business systems. Defences: multi-factor authentication, unique passwords and alerts for unusual sign-ins.

items.title: Insider risks
items.text: Harm caused deliberately or by mistake, such as sending data to the wrong person or keeping access after leaving. Defences: role-based access, access reviews and a leaver process.

items.title: Unpatched software
items.text: Attackers look for systems that have not applied released fixes. Defences: scheduled updates, a software inventory and regular vulnerability scans.

items.title: Misconfigured cloud services
items.text: Storage or services left open to the internet by mistake. Defences: configuration reviews, access restrictions and multi-factor authentication. See our [cloud services](/cloud-services).

items.title: Data exposure and breaches
items.text: Information seen, copied or taken by someone who should not have it. Defences: access controls, encryption, monitoring and a documented incident process.

items.title: Network-based threats
items.text: Attempts through open ports, weak remote access and unfiltered traffic. Defences: firewalls, segmentation, secure VPN access and intrusion detection.

faqs.q: What are cybersecurity services?
faqs.a: Cybersecurity services are activities that protect a business's systems, networks, devices and data from unauthorised access and damage. They include assessing risk, putting protective controls in place, monitoring for suspicious activity and preparing to respond to incidents.

faqs.q: Why do businesses need cybersecurity services?
faqs.a: Businesses need cybersecurity services because attacks target organisations of every size, and the cost of disruption or data loss is usually higher than the cost of prevention. Many businesses do not have in-house specialists, so an outside provider can assess risk, set up controls and keep them under review.

faqs.q: What is the difference between cybersecurity assessment and penetration testing?
faqs.a: A cybersecurity assessment identifies and ranks weaknesses and risks, while penetration testing is a controlled, authorised attempt to break into systems to show what an attacker could actually reach. Assessments are broader and are usually done first. Penetration testing is more specialised and is often used once basic weaknesses have been fixed.

faqs.q: What is vulnerability assessment in cybersecurity?
faqs.a: A vulnerability assessment is a structured check that finds known weaknesses in systems, networks and applications and ranks them by severity. It typically combines automated scanning with manual review, and it ends with a report of what to fix first. It identifies weaknesses but does not try to exploit them.

faqs.q: How can businesses reduce ransomware risks?
faqs.a: Businesses can reduce ransomware risk by combining several measures, because no single one is enough. Keep software and devices updated, use multi-factor authentication, limit who can access what, run endpoint protection, train staff to spot phishing and keep backups that are tested and stored apart from the main network. A written incident plan helps you respond quickly if an attack still succeeds.

faqs.q: What is the role of endpoint security?
faqs.a: Endpoint security protects the devices people use, such as laptops, desktops and mobile phones, from malware, ransomware and unauthorised use. Because these devices connect to email, websites and external storage, they are among the most common ways attackers get in. It usually covers protection software, updates, device settings and access controls.

faqs.q: What is identity and access management?
faqs.a: Identity and access management is the set of processes and tools that control who can sign in to your systems and what they are allowed to do. It typically includes multi-factor authentication, single sign-on, role-based permissions and reviews of who has access. It reduces the risk of unauthorised access but cannot remove it.

intro.title: Cloud Computing Solutions for Modern Businesses
paragraphs: Cloud computing services give businesses access to computing resources such as servers, storage, databases, networking and software over the internet, usually paid for according to use. Instead of buying and housing all your own equipment, you rent capacity from a cloud platform. Cloud services also cover the work around it: moving systems to the cloud, setting up and running the environment, securing it and planning for recovery.

Businesses adopt the cloud to add capacity without buying hardware, to let staff in different locations reach the same systems, to reduce time spent on physical servers or to launch new applications faster. These benefits are not automatic. They depend on how the environment is designed, how workloads are placed and how well it is managed afterwards.

Cloud migration and cloud management are different jobs. Migration is a project: moving applications, data and workloads to the cloud. Management is ongoing: running the environment, reviewing performance, controlling cost and keeping it secure after the move. Many businesses need both, in that order. The wider ongoing operation of your IT is covered by our [managed IT services](/managed-it-services), while this page focuses on the cloud itself.

RPO is how much recent data you can afford to lose; RTO is how long you can be without a system. Lower targets usually cost more to meet.

Planning how to scale up or down

solutions.title: Common Cloud Challenges Businesses Face
solutions.text: The cloud solves some problems but can create others if it is not planned and reviewed.

items.title: High infrastructure maintenance effort
items.text: Moving suitable workloads to the cloud shifts some patching and repair work to the provider, and good management keeps the rest organised.

items.title: Unplanned cloud spending

items.title: Performance issues

items.title: Poor resource utilization

items.title: Data backup concerns

items.title: Hybrid environment complexity
items.text: Clear documentation, secure links and agreed responsibilities keep on-premises and cloud systems manageable together.

items.title: Limited internal cloud expertise
items.text: An external team can fill gaps, support your people and give a second opinion on design decisions.

technologies.title: Cloud Models Explained: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and Deployment Types
technologies.text: No model is best for everyone. The right choice depends on your applications, your data, your budget and your skills.

items.title: IaaS
items.text: Virtual servers, storage and networks. You manage operating systems, applications, data and access; the provider manages hardware, data centres and virtualisation. Suits moving on-premises servers.

items.title: PaaS
items.text: A managed platform for building and running applications. You manage applications, data and access. Suits developers who want faster deployment with less server management.

items.title: SaaS
items.text: A finished application used over the internet. You manage users, access settings and data. Suits businesses that want a ready-made tool with the least maintenance.

items.title: Public cloud
items.text: Resources run by a provider and shared by many customers, each kept separate. Quick scaling and pay-for-use pricing, but costs can grow if unmanaged and your settings are your responsibility.

items.title: Private cloud
items.text: Resources dedicated to one organisation, on your premises or in a hosted facility. More control over data location, but higher upfront and maintenance cost.

items.title: Hybrid and multi-cloud
items.text: Hybrid combines private or on-premises resources with public cloud; multi-cloud uses more than one public provider. Both add operational complexity and need consistent access and security policies.

process.i0_text: We learn about your business, goals and competitors, and review your current website, search rankings, ads and social pages.
process.i1_text: We plan the channels, audience and budget, starting with the activities most likely to bring measurable results first.
process.i2_text: We set up the accounts and tracking, create the ads, posts and content, and launch with measurement in place from day one.
process.i3_text: We watch campaigns closely and adjust anything that underperforms early, instead of waiting for the monthly report.

costFactors.i0_text: SEO, paid ads, social media and content each have different costs depending on scope and effort.
costFactors.i1_text: Busy industries need more content, links and ad spend to stand out in search and social feeds.
costFactors.i2_text: A campaign with one clear goal costs less than a plan running on several platforms at once.
costFactors.i3_text: Choose a one-time project or a monthly plan. Every proposal shows what each part costs and what it should deliver.

mistakes.title: Running ads without tracking
mistakes.text: Without conversion tracking, there is no reliable way to know what a campaign is producing.
mistakes.fix: We set up tracking before any campaign goes live.

mistakes.title: Treating SEO and ads separately
mistakes.text: Search and paid campaigns learn from each other; running them apart wastes that insight.
mistakes.fix: We plan SEO and ads as one coordinated strategy.

mistakes.title: Content with no plan to reach people
mistakes.text: Great content that nobody sees rarely pays back the time spent creating it.
mistakes.fix: Every piece comes with a plan for where it will be shared.

mistakes.title: Sending ad traffic to the home page
mistakes.text: A generic page is one of the quickest ways to spend an ad budget without getting enquiries.
mistakes.fix: We build focused landing pages for each campaign.

mistakes.title: Chasing likes instead of leads
mistakes.text: Followers and impressions matter less than real enquiries and sales.
mistakes.fix: We report on leads, sales and cost per enquiry.
